messages:
acme-demo-user: Hey @support — during a demo this morning our org hit a hard zero across two projects at ~09:15 PT. We were mid-streaming on a long websocket and suddenly started getting 429s and "insufficient credits". Can you confirm when tenant monthly tokens actually refill?

emma (support): Sorry about that — can you paste the exact error response body and the tenant id? Also did you notice the UI showing 0 or were calls failing first?

acme-demo-user: Error payload: {
  "error": "quota_exhausted",
  "message": "monthly token bucket depleted"
}
We saw UI show 0 about 30s after the first 429s. Tenant id: org_9A1B2C. This happened after a long-running stream (~2.5 hours).

emma (support): Thanks — passing to infra. @tom can you check refill job logs + billing agg for org_9A1B2C?

tom (infra): Looking now. Quick note: refill job (billing-aggregator) runs daily to reconcile monthly buckets; there are two relevant jobs — refill-scheduler (fires at 00:05 UTC) and per-tenant reconcile which can touch persisted display state/cache. Any chance this tenant has a timezone override or an older bootstrapped tenant?

acme-demo-user: They created two projects in different regions but same org. No timezone overrides that I can see in the UI.

oncall-bot: Deploy notice: rolling patch deployed to ratesvc at 1763002200 (commit d4c3b2a). No rollbacks.

tom (infra): I pulled the logs. For org_9A1B2C the billing-agg reconciliation executed at 00:05 UTC, but the display-cache invalidation for that org showed a TTL eviction at 08:59:57 UTC which corresponds to 01:59:57 PT (PDT). That lines up with the reported 09:15 PT? Wait there's a DST shift mismatch.

sophia (billing): We track monthly cycles relative to the tenant creation timestamp (UTC) but display/UI uses tenant-local offsets for convenience. Looks like during the DST transition the UI offset drifted and showed 0 earlier than the backend reconciliation actually ran. That can cause customers to see 0 in the console while the backend still has credits (or vice versa).

emma (support): Summary so far: customer saw 429s mid-stream. Backend reconciliation completed earlier (or later) but UI cache invalidation + tenant local offset produced an apparent zero. Two action items: 1) temporary top-up to unblock customer, 2) fix to normalize refill time handling across DST and long-lived sockets. @tom assignable?

tom (infra): Assigning a short-term patch: normalize refill timestamps to use absolute UTC epoch for reconciliation + signal refresh for active websocket sessions. Patch deployed at 1763004000 (small signal hook). I'll roll an explicit cache purge for org_9A1B2C now.

oncall-bot: Cache purge executed for org_9A1B2C at 1763004100.

acme-demo-user: After the purge the stream resumed and errors stopped. Thanks. Can you explain root cause so we can report back to our PMs?

sophia (billing): Root cause (short): tenant monthly bucket reconciliation was timezone-accurate in backend, but the UI and streaming session state used a local offset value that didn't account for DST boundary in this tenant's region. For long-running websockets the session kept a local-visible counter that reached 0 earlier than the backend's authoritative bucket.

emma (support): Next steps: (1) Billing to add a short-term safety top-up policy for active demo orgs (sophia will file a follow-up), (2) Infra to post a durable fix to use UTC epoch for refill and push session refresh signals (tom tracked in INF-5342), (3) Support to notify customer and log postmortem.

acme-demo-user: Appreciate the quick turnaround. Leaving this thread open until INF-5342 lands. :white_check_mark:

emma (support): Noted — I'll follow up with a mitigation email and a temporary credit on the account. Marking thread for SLA follow-up. :eyes:
